summary: Iteration 84 tested map time (backend and frontend), the tile-only gate and the viewing hardening. Backend: test_map_time.py and test_viewings.py pass 9/9. The new suite against the public URL (tests/test_iter84_map_time_public.py) passes 5/6. These all work: the 0-MASS gate, the first hour charged once, the ledger row (spend_feature -1, feature_key map_time), GET /map/time being read-only, the hour rolling over, the empty-wallet gate, a top-up buying the next hour, gaps over 150 s accruing nothing, map_hour_mass=0 making the map free (and -1 returning 422), and the availability checks (99:99 → 400, overlap → 400, end before start → 400, adjacent windows → 200). The one failure is a HIGH race: parallel markers/tick calls each charge an hour (6 parallel calls → 5 MASS charged instead of 1). This can happen in the real app: coming back from an unlocked listing fires tick() and load() at the same moment. Regression: test_viewings_race_iter83 now fails every time (6 parallel POST /viewings → six 201s, so six duplicate open requests). Frontend at 390x844: everything requested works. That covers the zero-MASS gate (no pins, gate card, Get MASS → /buy-tokens, no count pill, no empty card, no chip), top-up → back → markers reload, the demo chip (60 min plus info toast), the locked pin's photo, body and primary taps each opening UnlockDialog while the URL stays '/', the unlocked pin's photo opening /property/{id}, the segments, the filter sheet, preview close, and the wallet row 'Map time · 60 min on Find Home · Feature -1'. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

critical.issue: Race causes double charging. tick() reads the map_time doc, checks used>=paid, debits, then upserts, with no atomic guard. Concurrent calls each see the hour as used up and each debit 1 MASS. Reproduced: a fresh user with 5 MASS and 6 parallel calls ended at 0 MASS, with charged_now=true on 5 of them. Real-app trigger: index.tsx useFocusEffect fires tick() (line ~405) and the openedRef effect fires load() → /map/markers (line ~442) at the same moment when returning from a listing. If the hour has run out, the user is charged 2 MASS.

Duplicate open requests on concurrent POST. request_viewing does find_one(existing open) and then inserts, with no unique index or lock. 6 parallel identical POSTs → six 201s (tests/test_viewings_race_iter83.py fails 2/2 runs). The viewings collection has no partial unique index on (buyer_id, property_id) for open statuses.

minor.issue: '24:00' is rejected (h>23), so an agent can't set a window that ends at midnight. Acceptable but worth noting.

3 tests in test_map_passport_redesign.py fail on data-dependent assertions unrelated to this iteration: demo unlocked ratio >0.5 (now 14/143); the FIXA user has 3 unlocked markers; KeyError 'approx' on the /property detail payload. test_review_map_monetization::test_map_markers_requires_auth_and_shape is the known stale failure.

integration_issues.issue: tick() and load() fire concurrently on focus. Together with the backend race above, this can charge 2 MASS for one hour. Fix it on the backend (atomic). Optionally also skip the focus tick when a silent load is about to run.

issues: The map-gate card (x 35–355, y ≈278–578) partly covers the fab-zoom-out button (x 330–378, y 312–360).
map-time-chip is 82x36, below the 44pt minimum touch target, and has no hitSlop.
On first load the ₦285M price pin sits on top of the fab-zoom-out button.

action_items: HIGH: Make MapTimeMeter.tick atomic. Use an optimistic CAS, e.g. find_one_and_update({user_id, hours_charged: hours, paid_seconds: paid}, {$set: {...new values}}), and debit ONLY if the CAS matched. Alternatively, debit with an idempotency reference such as f'map_time:{uid}:{hours+1}' using a unique index on wallet transactions, so concurrent charges for the same hour collapse into one. Re-run tests/test_iter84_map_time_public.py::test_concurrent_first_load_charges_once.

HIGH: Prevent duplicate open viewing requests. Add a partial unique index on viewings (buyer_id, property_id) with partialFilterExpression status in OPEN_STATUSES and catch DuplicateKeyError → 409. Re-run tests/test_viewings_race_iter83.py.
LOW: Keep the map-gate card from covering fab-zoom-out (narrower card or more top margin). Add hitSlop or a 44pt min height to map-time-chip.
LOW: Update the stale assertions in test_map_passport_redesign.py and test_review_map_monetization.py.
critical_code_review_comments: map_time.py: the check-then-debit-then-upsert pattern is not concurrency-safe (see critical). The unique index on map_time.user_id stops duplicate docs but not double debits.

map_time.py: a paid hour stays 'unused' forever while the user is away. So a user who bought an hour and then spent the rest of their MASS still sees markers with 0 MASS until the hour is used. This matches rule B, but it means rule A ('0 MASS → no markers') isn't strictly true. Make sure this is the intended product behaviour.
viewings.py request_viewing: the existing-open check and the agent-slot conflict (confirmed only) are both non-atomic.
PreviewCard / index.tsx onOpen routing is correct: locked → primaryAction → UnlockDialog, unlocked → openPin.

success_rate.backend: 83% of the new suite (5/6); 9/9 in the E1 suites; 52/57 in the related regression suites (1 real regression, 4 stale)

rca_of_issue: Map-time double charge: tick() is a read-modify-write with no atomicity. Two requests in flight both read used>=paid and both call wallet.debit. Reproduce: fresh user with 5 MASS, then 6 parallel GET /map/markers + POST /map/time/tick → balance 0. Fix: CAS on the map_time doc (or an idempotent debit keyed by hour number) before or with the debit. Viewing duplicates: same pattern in request_viewing (find_one existing → insert). Fix with a partial unique index.
